# Local agent testing

- Claude Code: run `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS=1000000 ccfree 3` to use the developer's local cloud-model setup.
- Codex: use the model already configured for this developer; do not change the model setting for tests.
- OpenCode: use the free `glm5.3` model.

These are local development choices, not ai-persona runtime defaults. Do not change an agent's built-in tools, modes, model settings, or permissions as part of the plugin.

# Git remote

- Keep `origin` set to `git@github.com:aminammar1/ai-persona.git`; use SSH for pushes and pulls, and do not switch this remote to HTTPS.

---
name: persona-init
description: Set up ai-persona for the current project and coding agent.
---

Scan the project and identify its stack. Read the bundled `references/profile-template.md`, prepare a project specific `profile.md`, and show it to the developer. Ask permission before writing the profile, fetching the runtime, installing dependencies, or changing agent configuration. After approval, locate `scripts/setup.mjs` beside this skill and run it with the current project path and agent name (`opencode`, `claude`, `codex`, or `omp`), plus `--approved`. The installer fetches the runtime over SSH, installs its dependencies, and registers the supported adapter and MCP server for OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex, or omp. Confirm that setup succeeded before saying the adapter is active.

For Codex, inspect `$CODEX_HOME/config.toml` (default `~/.codex/config.toml`) before setup. Current Codex uses `[features].hooks`; `codex_hooks` is a deprecated alias. Warn when the effective hooks flag is off, including when managed policy disables it. After setup, have the developer review and trust the hooks in `/hooks`. If hooks remain off or untrusted, say the adapter is inactive and do not imply that guards ran.

---
name: persona-learn
description: Review suggested ai-persona profile or rule updates.
---

Use `list_learning_suggestions` to show at most three pending suggestions with their evidence. Ask a separate yes/no for each and have the developer reply `yes <id>` or `no <id>`. Call `review_learning_suggestion` only after that exact reply; the OpenCode prompt hook records it and the tool requires it. Never infer approval or auto-apply. Mention `list_changes` and offer `undo_change` for applied entries. Rejecting or skipping makes no change.

---
name: persona-mode
description: Show or switch ai-persona's current state with one word.
---

Show the current state, or accept one state word: `init`, `flow`, `debug`, `explore`, or `careful`. Keep the developer's task unchanged. If no adapter is available, explain that the state change is only a request and do not claim it is active.

---
name: persona-rules
description: Add a standing order in the developer's own words.
---

Parse one requested order, such as “don't commit”, “don't push”, “don't touch these paths”, or “use this MCP”. Use `propose_guard` for supported rules, show the parsed rule once, and ask the developer to confirm. Call `confirm_guard` only after an explicit yes; reject it after a no. Never activate a rule without confirmation. Don't claim a guard blocks tool calls unless the current agent has a verified pre-tool hook wired to `checkGuard`.

# ai-persona

Your coding agent, shaped around how you work. Five states adapt its style to your project and prompts while keeping your task intact. Hooks check tool calls. Memory stores short notes, never transcripts. ## How it works

The profile sets your baseline. State hints appear only on changes. A one word override works, and built in modes and permissions stay in control. See [agent coverage and hook gaps](docs/agent-hooks.md). ## Demo Real output from a live OpenCode run in a Go test project, captured with `opencode run`. **One word changes the state.** A bare `careful` prompt rewrites the stored state: ```json { "lastState": "careful", "settingsKey": "{\"verbosity\":\"balanced\",\"autonomy\":\"ask\",\"caution\":\"high\",\"exploration\":\"balanced\"}" } ``` **Hints ride along invisibly.** The prompt stored in the OpenCode session database keeps your exact text, no persona line appended. The agent still quotes the system note verbatim: ``` Persona flow: verbosity balanced, autonomy act, caution balanced, exploration balanced. act on the task and keep updates brief. Keep the developer's task unchanged; respect active agent modes, tools, and permissions. ``` **Standing orders block tool calls before they run.** After confirming a `don't push` guard, `git push origin main` fails before executing: ``` Error: Blocked by standing order: don't push. ``` **Habits surface as short nudges** at the end of file tool results: ``` Created file successfully: nudge-test.txt Profile habit: After changing code, run make test before claiming success. ``` And `get_persona` stays compact, 137 characters in this run: ``` Baseline dials: verbosity balanced, autonomy act, caution balanced, exploration balanced. Where we left off: No open problem was recorded. ``` ## Install ```bash npx skills add aminammar1/ai-persona ``` Install all four skills, open your project in the agent, then run `persona-init`. It scans the project, creates `profile.md`, shows the setup plan, and asks before installing hooks and MCP. ## Contribute PRs are welcome for a stack template, persona preset, or agent adapter. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## License [MIT](LICENSE) © 2026 Mohamed Amine Ammar.

# Contributing

PRs are welcome for:

* A project stack profile template under `templates/`.
* A persona preset that adjusts how the agent works without changing the task.
* An adapter for an agent with documented hooks.

For adapter changes, link the agent's current official hook documentation and document unsupported hooks or tool paths. Keep enforcement in hooks or tools, preserve the agent's built in permissions and modes, and keep learning suggest only. No transcript storage, tests, or CI are part of this project.

Run `npm run typecheck` before opening a PR. Include a short usage example and note any setup or hook coverage limits.

# Verified agent hooks

These lists come from the official docs read on 2026-11-06 and re-verified on 2026-11-13 (OpenCode v2 server plugin docs and oh-my-pi 18 extension docs against the installed typings and binary). Hook availability and behavior can change; check the linked docs again before implementing an adapter. A listed event is not a promise that every adapter can enforce every rule through it.

After the developer approves setup, `persona-init` fetches the runtime into `.ai-persona/runtime`, installs its dependencies, and adds the current agent's hook and MCP configuration to the project. It does not change built in modes, tools, or permissions.

## OpenCode v2.2.5

`opencode --version` reported `opencode v2.2.5`. The official v2 plugin API exposes these hooks:

- Tool: `execute.before`, `execute.after`.
- Shell: `create.before`.
- Permission: `evaluate`.
- Session: `prompt`, `context`, `compaction`, `generate`, `title`, `model.request`, `http.request`, `http.response`, `experimental.ws.handshake`, `experimental.ws.send`, `experimental.ws.receive`, `retry`, `experimental.idle`.
- AI SDK: `sdk`, `language`.

The per-prompt hook is `ctx.session.hook("prompt", ...)`. It sees an incoming user prompt once at admission, before attachment and skill resolution. It does not see synthetic messages, shell messages, compaction controls, or move controls. The adapter runs the detector there and never modifies the prompt text, so the developer's message is stored exactly as sent. Repeated prompts are recognized with short project state fingerprints; prompt text is not retained. A user interruption sets the next prompt to debug.

State hints are injected invisibly instead: a `ctx.session.hook("context", ...)` hook appends the current state's one-line hint to the system parts of every agent-loop model call, so the hint rides with each request and its continuations without ever appearing in the stored conversation. Subagent child sessions (created with a parent session) are skipped. The current hint is cached in memory per project and refreshed on every prompt; if the cache is cold (for example after a restart), the hook recomputes it read-only from the saved state and never writes.

`ctx.event.subscribe()` exposes lifecycle events including `session.created`, `session.execution.interrupted`, `session.idle`, `permission.asked`, `permission.replied`, and `session.compaction.ended`. The compaction ended event includes the generated summary text, so the adapter requests labeled decision, correction, and open problem sections and stores only those bullets. `session.compacted` is not an event name in the v2.2.5 API. `file.edited` is also absent from the v2 API; `filesystem.changed` is a different event, so the adapter uses successful file tool results for its habit nudge.

The adapter uses `ctx.tool.hook("execute.before", ...)` for guards and `execute.after` to add the profile's habit nudge to successful file-tool results. The v2 file tools are `edit`, `write`, and `patch` (v2 renamed the v1 `apply_patch` tool to `patch`); patch paths are read from the `patchText` markers. It records user interruptions and paired permission replies in project SQLite. Reviewed permission preferences are stored as project notes only; the adapter does not change OpenCode's built-in permission decisions. The TUI plugin listens to `session.idle`, showing an in-app toast and a system notification when OpenCode is blurred.

Sources: [Plugin overview](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins/), [Server plugin API](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins/server), [TUI plugin API](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins/cli/), [MCP servers and tool names](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/mcp-servers).

## Claude Code

The current reference exposes: `SessionStart`, `Setup`, `InstructionsLoaded`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `UserPromptExpansion`, `MessageDisplay`, `PreToolUse`, `PermissionRequest`, `PostToolUse`, `PostToolUseFailure`, `PostToolBatch`, `PermissionDenied`, `Notification`, `SubagentStart`, `SubagentStop`, `TaskCreated`, `TaskCompleted`, `Stop`, `StopFailure`, `TeammateIdle`, `ConfigChange`, `CwdChanged`, `DirectoryAdded`, `FileChanged`, `WorktreeCreate`, `WorktreeRemove`, `PreCompact`, `PostCompact`, `PreModelSwitch`, `PostModelSwitch`, `SessionEnd`, `Elicitation`, and `ElicitationResult`.

The installer merges `SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `Stop`, `PreCompact`, and `PostCompact` from `hooks/hooks.json` into the project's `.claude/settings.json`. The shared TypeScript handler initializes the state, classifies each submitted prompt, checks supported tool calls before execution, adds the profile nudge after successful file tools, and emits a completion message at `Stop` with system message output. The adapter does not register `PermissionRequest` or `PermissionDenied`: the API exposes permission asks and denials, but no hook reports the user's approval reply, so the events cannot be paired into a complete record. `PreCompact` asks for labeled durable facts; `PostCompact` parses those sections and stores only their bullets.

Claude's current `PreToolUse` hook covers built-in and MCP tool calls, except `EndConversation`; prompt `@` file mentions can also bypass tool hooks. The adapter only recognizes common path argument names, so a custom tool with an unrecognized path field is outside protected-path enforcement. `PostToolUse` fires after successful tool calls, and this adapter listens only for file tools; shell or external file writes do not trigger its habit nudge. Claude has no interruption event.

Sources: [Hooks reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks), [Plugin components and hooks](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/components).

## Codex

The current reference exposes: `SessionStart`, `SessionEnd`, `SubagentStart`, `SubagentStop`, `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `PreCompact`, `PostCompact`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `Stop`, `Interrupt`, `PermissionRequest`, `PreModelRequest`, and `PostModelRequest`.

The compatibility manifest explicitly points to `hooks/codex-hooks.json`. The installer merges `SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `Stop`, and `Interrupt` into the project's `.codex/hooks.json`, and adds the MCP server to `.codex/config.toml`. The `Interrupt` entry sets `"timeout": 3`, the maximum Codex allows, because interrupt hooks otherwise get a 1 second default. Codex's current feature key is `[features].hooks`; `codex_hooks` is a deprecated alias. Project `.codex` settings load only after the developer trusts that project; until then, project hooks and the project MCP entry do not load. Review the hook definitions with `/hooks` and trust them before relying on the adapter. `persona-init` warns during setup when the project is not marked trusted and when hooks are disabled; it does not change project trust, model settings, or built in permissions.

In an earlier local Codex CLI 0.167.0 smoke run, the project MCP entry did not respond during the session; the verified cause was that the project was not yet marked trusted, so Codex loaded no project `.codex` layer at all. An interim, temporary global MCP entry exposed `get_persona`, but Codex refused the call because the session approval policy was `never`; that temporary entry was removed. The adapter does not change project trust or Codex approval policy. Verify MCP access in a trusted interactive project session before relying on memory tools.

The adapter initializes state, classifies prompts, checks supported tool calls before execution, nudges after successful `apply_patch`/edit tools, records main-thread interruptions, and emits a completion message at `Stop`. Current Codex tool hooks cover Bash, `apply_patch`, MCP tools, and most local function tools, but not hosted tools such as web search; specialized paths can opt out. A tool using an unrecognized path argument is outside protected-path enforcement. Hook process failures and timeouts are not an enforcement guarantee, so callers must see an explicit denial response for a guard to block. `PermissionRequest` reports that approval is being requested, but no hook reports the user's approval reply, so the adapter does not register it. `PostCompact` reports only the trigger, not the compacted summary, so Codex cannot save structured compaction memory without reading its transcript. The adapter deliberately leaves that feature off.

Sources: [Codex hooks](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks), [Codex plugin packaging](https://developers.openai.com/plugins/build/plugins).

## omp (oh-my-pi 18.20.0)

`omp --version` reported `omp/18.20.0`. omp auto-discovers TypeScript extensions from `<cwd>/.omp/extensions` (project, cwd-only and gitignore-aware) and `~/.omp/agent/extensions` (user). `persona-init` symlinks the adapter module `hooks/omp-extension.ts` to `.omp/extensions/ai-persona.ts`; the module imports the shared core from the runtime clone and types omp's API structurally, importing no `@oh-my-pi` package.

- `session_start` resets project state for reasons `startup` and `new` (`ctx.cwd` is the project root); `reload`, `resume`, `fork`, and `revive` keep the stored state.
- `before_agent_start` fires for ordinary prompts and user steering batches in every mode, including print mode. The adapter classifies the prompt and returns a `systemPrompt` override that appends the current state's hint; the override governs that request and its continuations until the next prompt prepares policy, and it is never stored as user input, so the sent prompt stays untouched. `revive` (parked-subagent rebind, empty prompt) returns early. Task/subagent and advisor sessions (`ctx.agent.kind === "sub"`) are skipped in every handler.
- `tool_call` blocks standing-order violations before execution with `{ block: true, reason }`. omp names MCP tools `mcp__<server>_<tool>` (single underscore separator), so the extension derives the server name from the tool name; the built-in file tools are `edit`, `write`, and `apply_patch`, whose inputs use `filePath` and a `patch` body parsed for `*** Add|Update|Delete File:` and `*** Move to:` markers.
- `tool_result` returns the profile habit nudge as passive `additionalContext` after successful file tools; omp drops duplicate context inside one batch.
- `session.compacting` adds the labeled Decisions/Corrections/Open problems instructions to the summarizer context.

Known omp gaps: omp exposes no verified user-interruption event, so the interrupted → debug classification never triggers there; the `session_compact` payload is unverified, so compaction bullets are not recorded into project memory; and no permission ask/reply pairing hook is verified, so permission learning is OpenCode-only. `tool_call` fails closed on extension errors and on timeout (30 s default), so a broken store blocks calls until it is fixed.

The MCP server is registered in `.omp/mcp.json`, omp's native project-level MCP file (`mcpServers` map with `type: "stdio"`, `command`, `args`, `cwd`, `env`). `persona-init` writes the entry there and warns when `.omp` is gitignored, because native extension discovery skips gitignored paths.

Sources: [Extensions](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/main/docs/extensions.md), [Extension loading](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/main/docs/extension-loading.md), [MCP configuration](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/main/docs/mcp-config.md).

# Project memory and MCP tools

The local MCP server speaks stdio; stdout is reserved for MCP messages. `persona-init` registers it for the selected agent and sets the current project root explicitly. It writes memory to `.ai-persona/memory.sqlite`.

## Stored data

- `memories` stores concise decisions, corrections, and open problems. Repeated identical notes increment an occurrence count.
- `suggestions` stores proposed profile or rule changes with `pending` status. Proposals never edit the profile or agent configuration.
- There is no transcript table. `recordCompactionSummary()` accepts only structured arrays of decisions, corrections, and open problems; it truncates each saved note to 240 characters. Each compaction replaces the open-problem snapshot, so resolved problems do not reappear as the next session's handoff note.

Each project's database is in that project's directory. `get_persona(task)` cannot select a different project; it returns the current project's baseline, a small task-relevant profile slice, and at most three short notes. Its response is capped at 800 characters. The newest open problem supplies the “where we left off” note. No prior-project memory is consulted.

## Tools

- `get_persona(task)`: return baseline dials, matching profile headings and an optional matching file under `profile/`, plus at most three notes.
- `record_correction(note)`: save one concise correction for the current project.
- `propose_update(change)`: save a pending suggestion; approval is still required before anyone applies it.
- `propose_guard(rule)` and `confirm_guard(proposalId, accepted)`: parse a supported standing order, show its meaning once, then activate it only after explicit confirmation.
- `list_learning_suggestions()`: return at most three pending, evidence-backed suggestions.
- `review_learning_suggestion(suggestionId, approved)`: explicitly apply one narrow change or reject it.
- `list_changes()` and `undo_change(changeId)`: inspect recent applied changes and undo one without deleting its log entry.

`recordCompactionSummary(projectRoot, summary)` stores structured decisions, corrections, and the complete current open problem list. OpenCode reads the generated text from `session.compaction.ended`; Claude Code instructs compaction to emit labeled sections and reads `compact_summary` from `PostCompact`. Both store only bullets under those headings. Codex `PostCompact` exposes only the trigger, so Codex compaction saving remains unavailable without reading a transcript. The omp adapter adds the same labeled-section instructions through its `session.compacting` context, but omp's `session_compact` payload is unverified, so compaction bullets are not stored for omp. Prompt repetition state stores only three SHA 256 fingerprints in the project's state file and resets at a new session; prompt text is not retained.

## Standing-order guards

Confirmed guards are stored in the same project-local SQLite file and are checked by `checkGuard(projectRoot, call)` before an adapter runs a tool. Supported forms are `don't commit`, `don't push`, `don't touch <path>[, <path>...]`, and `use this MCP <name>`. A required-MCP guard blocks calls to other MCP servers; it leaves non-MCP tools alone. The check does not depend on persona state. Matching calls receive one single-line reason. Adapters must normalize tool identity, MCP server identity, shell command text, and target paths before calling it.

The OpenCode v2 plugin at `.opencode/plugins/ai-persona/` checks confirmed rules in the `execute.before` tool hook and raises OpenCode's `Tool.Error` with a one-line reason before execution. It selects the database using the current session location. Guards run regardless of persona state. If the store or adapter check fails, the hook blocks the call rather than letting an unchecked call run. The omp extension at `hooks/omp-extension.ts` checks the same rules in its `tool_call` event and blocks before execution with `{ block: true, reason }`; omp fails tool calls closed when an extension handler errors or times out. It derives the MCP server identity from omp's `mcp__<server>_<tool>` tool naming. `persona-init` installs the runtime into `.ai-persona/runtime`, links this plugin into `.opencode/plugins/` (or the omp extension into `.omp/extensions/`), and registers the MCP server for the selected agent. Claude Code and Codex call `hooks/agent-hook.ts` from their project hook configuration. Their verified hook coverage and gaps are listed in [agent-hooks.md](agent-hooks.md).

OpenCode loads this local plugin automatically. Its v2 API does not expose `session.compacted`; it exposes `session.compaction.ended` with the generated summary text. The plugin adds a short structured handoff request to the real `compaction` session hook, then stores only labeled bullets from the completed summary.

## Learning from repeated signals

The SQLite store counts identical corrections, user-caused `session.execution.interrupted` events, and paired permission requests. Permission pairing exists only in the OpenCode adapter, whose `permission.asked` and `permission.replied` events carry both sides of a permission decision; the Claude Code and Codex hook APIs have a permission-ask hook but no approval-reply hook, so their adapters do not record permission events, and omp has no verified permission hook. Suggestions require at least two identical corrections or interruptions. Permission suggestions require at least two exact `once` approvals for the same action and single resource, with no rejection. `always` replies are recorded but never suggested again because OpenCode already has that native saved approval. Wildcards, multiple resources, project-root permissions, directories, paths outside the project, and unrecognized resource types are excluded.

Signal detection only creates pending suggestions. The OpenCode prompt hook records only an exact developer reply of `yes <suggestionId>` or `no <suggestionId>`; the review tool refuses to change anything without that matching one-use confirmation. Supported applied changes are learned habits, a low-verbosity debug adjustment, a narrow “never run” command guard, and a recorded permission preference. That preference is a project note only; the plugin never changes the agent's built-in permission settings. Every applied change stores its action and target in `applied_changes`; `undo_change` removes that exact learned effect and retains the log record. `list_changes(beforeId)` pages through the full log three entries at a time. `get_persona` includes at most one approved habit within its existing three-note budget.
